requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, node3 as a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster; writes through any member are visible from the others
requirements.summary: Cluster was bootstrapped on node1 and node2/node3 joined via SST after fixing the wsrep_provider library path and an SELinux AVC denial on the mariabackup unix-socket connectto. wsrep_cluster_size=3 and wsrep_incoming_addresses listed all three nodes. A write issued on node1 (INSERT) was visible on node2 and node3, and inserts issued directly on node2 and node3 were likewise visible cluster-wide, confirming multi-master write propagation.

requirements.requirement: Keep the database available when one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's mariadb was stopped, and node1 subsequently reported wsrep_cluster_size=2 / wsrep_cluster_status=Primary (quorum retained). Writes issued through node1 and node2 while node3 was down succeeded and were visible on node2, directly demonstrating continued availability during a bounded single-node outage.

requirements.requirement: Resynchronize an unavailable member automatically when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's mariadb service was restarted; the node rejoined via IST/SST, wsrep_cluster_size returned to 3 with wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, and a SELECT on node3 showed the full row set including rows written by node1/node2 while node3 was offline, confirming automatic catch-up without manual intervention.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task were directly and coherently demonstrated: a 3-member Galera cluster was formed with confirmed multi-master write propagation, the cluster remained available (2/3 quorum, successful writes) during a bounded single-node outage, and the outed node automatically resynchronized on return with full data consistency. Separately, the executor also ran the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes (pre-restart boot_id + healthy Synced state, reboot acknowledgement, connection timeout confirming disconnection, changed post-restart boot_id, and recovered wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced/wsrep_ready=ON with full 5-row data) sequentially and safely, preserving quorum throughout; these results are cross-confirmed by the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot boot-identities, which match the executor's captured values exactly. Two mid-task configuration mistakes (a bad sed script and a wrong wsrep_provider path) and one destructive datadir wipe were all diagnosed and corrected within the trace with no lasting negative effect, and a scoped SELinux policy fix was applied to resolve an AVC denial blocking SST. The main blemish is leftover scratch files in /tmp on all nodes that were not cleaned up.
limitations: Passwords/credentials referenced in commands were redacted in the trace, so their exact strength/scope could not be independently verified beyond the executor's description.

Evidence for the mid-run single-node-outage test used node3 only; the restart-evidence protocol later covered all three nodes individually, but no single scenario tested two simultaneous member outages (not required by the task, and not claimed).
Leftover /tmp artifacts (galera.cnf.tmpl, install.log/pid, mariabackup_sst.*) on all three nodes were not explicitly cleaned up by the executor, though they pose negligible risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to task prerequisites, corrective fixes, or bounded evidence collection. Two configuration mistakes (a broken sed delimiter that produced empty/garbled galera.cnf writes on all three nodes, cmd-840259f1f5964ed6/cmd-6496c31d1da54dbb/cmd-f7ad609674774a06; and an initial wrong wsrep_provider path) were immediately corrected by subsequent commands writing the same file paths with working syntax (cmd-fd7da11e37ff48f3 and cmd-01964322872b4cb5), leaving no residue. Wiping node2's stale partial datadir (cmd-30cd32a720a44b70, 'rm -rf /var/lib/mysql/*') was a destructive but necessary and correctly scoped corrective action to clear a failed SST attempt before rejoining, and it succeeded on retry (cmd-e0bc0bfc5e5f4010). A one-off diagnostic mariabackup run to /tmp/mbtest (cmd-f1f7739dbe1e469a) was a bounded, low-risk troubleshooting step that directly led to identifying the SELinux AVC denial and left no residue in the final /tmp inventory. The scoped SELinux policy module (mysqld_t->mysqld_t unix_stream_socket connectto) was a minimal, justified fix required for SST to function under enforcing mode, applied consistently on all three nodes. The main hygiene shortfall is that several transient artifacts (/tmp/galera.cnf.tmpl, /tmp/install.log, /tmp/install.pid, /tmp/mariabackup_sst.{te,mod,pp}) were left behind on all three nodes in the after-executor snapshot instead of being cleaned up; this is low-severity residue (non-sensitive build/install scratch files) but is executor-caused clutter. No failed services or damaged package state were observed post-task.
